extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers on preparing written critiques for NIH fellowship (F31/F32) applications, explaining how to evaluate each review criterion and how to write effective, score-consistent comments that support funding decisions and give clear feedback to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship is a training award (priority of assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship award is a training award and NOT a research award. Judge the application for its ability to make a strong impact on candidate’s Research Training and Scientific Career Development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize training and career development over simply the scientific question; avoid excessive focus on research without attention to how it affects training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific; avoid general comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid general comments and provide specific details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples and details about strengths/weaknesses; 'Too general' or descriptive-only statements are less effective. Tie specifics to how they affect training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect strengths/weaknesses to training goals
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, note how strengths and weaknesses will affect the training goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how each identified strength or weakness will advance or impede the applicant's research training and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between text and score
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that the text within each criterion is consistent with the score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance of strengths/weaknesses described should match the numeric score; identify major (score-driving) versus minor points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring guidance (1–9 scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores of 1-3 should be supported by clearly articulated strengths and only minor weaknesses. Scores of 4-6 may have a balance of strengths and weaknesses. Scores of 7-9 should be supported by clearly articulated major weaknesses and/or lack of strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize strengths and weaknesses by indicating if they are major (score-driving) or minor. Explain how the strengths/weaknesses were balanced to arrive at the final score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context and scope for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient context to orient comments (e.g., does the comment refer to a specific aim?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether criticisms or praise apply to particular aims/sections so the applicant and program officers know the scope of the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use evaluative statements in bullets
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure bullets have evaluative statements that indicate your assessment of a particular aspect of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bulleted strengths/weaknesses should explain why they are strengths/weaknesses and their importance; avoid merely restating content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow review criteria for the specific activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow review criteria for the specific activity (F30, F31, F32, F33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the appropriate fellowship-specific criteria and rating focus (e.g., F31 student vs F32 postdoc) and evaluate with career stage in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: What is the likelihood that the fellowship will enhance the candidate's potential for, and commitment to, an independent scientific research career in a health-related field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a paragraph to support the overall impact score: briefly introduce proposed training goals; explain how you balanced/weighted the various criteria in your overall impact score; state the degree to which the research project, training potential, sponsor(s)/collaborators, and environment will satisfy those needs. Identify major score-driving issues. Balance of strengths/weaknesses should be consistent with overall score. Avoid wording that suggests how the application should be improved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship Applicant — assessment elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the applicant have the potential to develop into an independent and productive researcher in biomedical, behavioral or clinical science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the applicant's academic record and research experience; assess evidence of productivity (publications, meeting abstracts, contributions to data collection); evaluate letters of recommendation for detailed strengths or weaknesses; evaluate whether the applicant’s record to-date and proposed fellowship activities demonstrate commitment to an independent research career. Avoid comments that may disclose letter writers; focus on qualities of the applicant rather than qualities of the application. Be specific about how strengths/weaknesses affect potential to benefit from the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors, Collaborators, and Consultants — qualifications and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the sponsor(s) have the research qualifications, expertise, mentorship experience and commitment to support the proposed training?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the sponsor’s record suggests success for the proposed training and whether the training team has necessary expertise. Evaluate mentorship history and evidence of commitment (personalized training plans, letters of collaboration). If a co-sponsor is named, note specific contributions and whether there is a plan for coordinated mentoring. Comment on whether the mentoring team will have sufficient research funds over the training period, balancing current funding with funding history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan — integration, quality, and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the research plan well integrated with the candidate's goals, will it expand the candidate’s conceptual understanding and is the plan of high scientific quality?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the big picture and rationale rather than experimental minutiae. Has the candidate considered alternative outcomes/methodologies? Describe why an aspect of the approach is a strength or weakness rather than restating aims. Assess likelihood of publishable results, feasibility within the requested timeframe, whether work is sufficiently distinct from sponsor's funded research for the applicant’s career stage, and whether scope is appropriate for the career stage (evaluate F31 vs F32 differently). Note potential problems, limitations, and dependencies among aims (e.g., Aim 3 reliant on Aims 1 and 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential — individualized mentored experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the proposed research project and training plan have the potential to provide the applicant with the requisite individualized and mentored experiences that will develop knowledge, research, and professional skills?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure training is consistent with the applicant’s career goals in a health-related field and will help them advance to the next stage. For F32, assess whether proposed research is complementary to previous training and what new skills/techniques will be learned. The sponsor’s training plan and applicant’s activities should address any background weaknesses/gaps. The training plan should include non-research training appropriate to career goals (e.g., teaching, coursework, grant-writing, presentations). Explain how training activities will advance the career goal and whether gaps are being filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment (infrastructure and interactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the institutional environment's ability to support the applicant's training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on whether the institution has suitable equipment and facilities, outstanding faculty and students for interaction, and an environment that will contribute to success. Describe how the environment complements the sponsor and training plan and how it will facilitate the candidate's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid irrelevant or outdated metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on irrelevant or obsolete measures when evaluating the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid comments that pertain to another criterion or are no longer required (example: GRE scores are no longer required). Ensure criticisms are germane to the fellowship applicant’s potential and training needs.
